maria: Heads up — the HF->Redwood conversion dropped repetition_penalty for a new model bring-up (gpt-small-3). Quick repro below, original generation_config.json had rep_penalty but runtime call didn't.

maria: ```json
{
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "top_k": 40,
  "repetition_penalty": 1.2,
  "eos_token_id": 50256
}
```

devon: I can confirm. Our conversion pipeline currently filters unknown keys and "normalizes" values against Redwood defaults. Bug: we accidentally treat any numeric field equal to the runtime default as "missing" and drop it, but somehow rep_penalty > 1.0 got nulled in some code path. Example converted payload we saw: `{"temperature":0.7,"top_p":0.9,"top_k":40}` (no repetition_penalty).

zheng: Also saw tokenizer mismatch on that model — HF config reports `eos_token_id: 2` but the tokenizer's special token text is "" and our wrapper maps it to 50256 fallback. That can cause early termination if the model expects a different EOS.

maria: That explains some hallucination/early-stop regressions in chat evals. We saw more truncated responses in the initial quantized runs.

sophie: FWIW, in int8 experiments we saw a slight uptick in unexpected EOS tokens mid-response; could be quantization affecting logits around the eos token id boundary. Worth verifying with non-quantized baseline.

eval-bot: added failing test: `tests/test_genconfig_mapping.py::test_preserve_repetition_penalty` — failure: expected repetition_penalty 1.2 to be forwarded to runtime payload, got None.

maria: Proposed fixes: 1) preserve any keys explicitly present in generation_config.json (do not drop numeric keys just because they equal a documented default). 2) explicitly map special token strings via tokenizer: call `tokenizer.eos_token` / `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids` and prefer that id if present. 3) emit a warning in conversion logs when eos_token_id in config != tokenizer.eos_token_id. 4) add a small eval that compares output length/perplexity before/after mapping to catch regressions.

devon: I'll draft a PR. Also let's add a rule: if both `top_k` and `top_p` are present, keep both but prefer `top_p` for sampling ordering in runtime; log the decision. Some teams rely on both being set for legacy models.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging canary scheduled 2025-02-12T14:30:00Z for branch genconfig/fix-rep-penalty

devon: Opened PR #1987: branch `genconfig/fix-rep-penalty`. Changes: preserve explicit numeric fields, normalize special tokens using tokenizer API, add unit+integration tests, and add a conversion log line showing original vs mapped values. Also added an integration check that runs the quantized ONNX model on 50 chat turns and compares truncation rate.

maria: Awesome — can you also add a tiny doc blurb in docs/model-onboarding.md about special token expectations and recommended generation_config keys we require?

devon: Yep. PR includes a docs paragraph and the test harness entry.

sophie: :thumbsup:

maria: After merge, I'll re-run the wikitext ppl and chat BLEU sweep on the staging canary and report numbers here.

eval-bot: CI: tests passed except flaky test `test_tokenizer_roundtrip` — rerunning.

devon: Thanks everyone — will tag you on the PR for review.
